unknowns: F4 VERDICT (measured, not open): the flash is SETTINGS-PAGE ONLY. The global banner does not flash - index.html:16 and :20 ship the banner divs with style='display:none', and main.js only ever applies real values from /api/settings/public, so the global path fails CLOSED. SettingsTab never calls applyBanner() before its fetch resolves either (mounted -> loadSettings -> await -> applyBanner at :49). What DOES flash is the Settings PANE: the template renders the seeded data() defaults immediately, so the Preview swatch at :203-205 shows green/UNCLASSIFIED and the form controls at :184-198 show wrong values until the fetch lands. There is no loading gate. THE REAL BUG IS WORSE THAN THE FLASH: loadSettings returns early at :42 when the response is not ok (an expired session, say), leaving the seeded defaults in place; the user's next toggle calls saveBanner() at :59, which PUTs bannerText/bannerBg/bannerFg straight from data() - overwriting the operator's real saved banner with green/UNCLASSIFIED for every user globally. Cosmetic flash and silent data loss share one root cause: defaults seeded into the same fields the save path reads.

D-1 PRIVILEGE MECHANISM (recommendation, needs sign-off) - all three options in the brief were tested on prod and the results decide it. NoNewPrivileges=true genuinely blocks sudo: 'sudo: The "no new privileges" flag is set, which prevents sudo from running as root', while the control run with NoNewPrivileges=no reached 'a password is required'. So the sudoers approach is dead as the unit stands. ProtectSystem=strict makes /etc read-only for the service ('Read-only file system' on /etc/topic-manager). polkit IS installed (polkitd 124) and `systemctl start topic-manager.service` run as topic-manager under NoNewPrivileges=yes failed with 'Interactive authentication required' - a POLKIT denial, not an NNP denial. That proves the D-Bus manage-units path survives NoNewPrivileges, because the caller never escalates: it asks PID 1 to act. RECOMMENDATION: option (b) polkit, with a rule matching subject.user == 'topic-manager' and action.lookup('unit') in exactly {topic-manager.service, nginx.service} plus a verb allowlist, returning polkit.Result.YES. It needs no unit change, no sudoers, and no new Python dependency (the systemctl CLI is the client); it keeps NoNewPrivileges and ProtectSystem=strict intact; and every authorisation is journald-logged by polkitd. Trade-off against (c), the .path-unit watcher: polkit grants the app user a standing capability, so any code-execution bug in the app can restart those two units, whereas (c) grants nothing and keeps the decision root-side at the cost of two more unit files and a marker-file protocol. Both are acceptable; (b) is fewer moving parts and is the one I would ship.

D-2 ATOMIC WRITE (recommendation, needs sign-off) - the decided layout has a problem that must be settled before builder starts. Measured: with clusters.yaml owned topic-manager:topic-manager 0640 inside /etc/topic-manager (root:topic-manager 0750) and ReadWritePaths naming the FILE, in-place write WORKS but atomic replace is IMPOSSIBLE (cannot create a temp file in the dir), so every save is truncate-then-write and loses the whole cluster list if interrupted - and with 4 workers two concurrent saves can interleave. The obvious fix is fatal: making the directory group-writable was tested, and the app user UNLINKED a root-owned 0600 secrets file purely via directory write permission. Chained with F1 that is a full auth-config takeover: delete config.yaml, write a new one with an attacker-chosen required_group, restart. RECOMMENDATION: give the file its own subdirectory, /etc/topic-manager/clusters.d/ owned topic-manager:topic-manager 0750, with ReadWritePaths=/etc/topic-manager/clusters.d. Atomic rename works inside it, and /etc/topic-manager itself stays root-owned and non-writable so config.yaml cannot be unlinked. This changes the path the operator specified, so it needs an explicit yes.

ANSWER to the brief's direct question - does adding /etc/topic-manager to ReadWritePaths re-open the secrets file? NO, measured twice: with ReadWritePaths=/etc/topic-manager the app still got 'Permission denied' creating a file in the dir (group has r-x, not w) and 'Permission denied' appending to config.yaml (0640 root:topic-manager gives the app read, not write). DAC holds independently of the mount namespace, so the split does what it is meant to. But the app must keep READ on config.yaml - that is how it loads secret_key - so the split protects against WRITE, not against read-based disclosure. Which is exactly why the cert-path oracle matters.

CERT/KEY UPLOAD - where they live, who owns them, and what stops ssl_keyfile: /etc/shadow. RECOMMENDATION: /opt/topic-manager/data/cluster-certs/, dir 0700 topic-manager:topic-manager, files 0600. That path is ALREADY inside the unit's ReadWritePaths, so it needs no sandbox change at all, and it is outside /etc so no secrets directory is opened. What stops an arbitrary path is not validating a path - it is never accepting one: the API takes uploaded CONTENT, parses it as PEM before storing, generates the filename server-side from the cluster id plus a random suffix, and persists only that generated path. The user-facing fields become uploads, not text boxes. Belt and braces: on load, realpath every ssl_* value and refuse anything not under the cert dir, so a hand-edited clusters file cannot reintroduce the oracle either. Note /etc/shadow is a red herring - the app cannot read it. The file that matters is config.yaml, which it can.

MULTI-WORKER STALENESS - the brief names _config_cache; there are TWO caches, and fixing one looks like success. tm/config.py:5 _config_cache returns early forever, and tm/app.py:31 freezes a second copy into app.config which tm/routes.py:39 _cfg() hands to every route. Even a correct in-process invalidation reaches 1 of 4 workers (4 gunicorn workers measured live on prod), so a newly added cluster would appear on roughly 1 request in 4 - intermittent, and it will read as a Kafka problem. RECOMMENDATION: give the clusters file its own load with an mtime+size check on every read so all 4 workers converge with no IPC, and change _cfg() to call that accessor instead of returning the frozen dict. Worth an explicit adversary test: add a cluster, then hit /api/clusters 20 times and require 20 identical responses.

ROLE SEPARATION - the contract's own principle is that every authenticated user is a Kafka admin and there is no role separation. F1 and F2 hand every Kafka-Admins member the ability to restart the service and rewrite the cluster list. That is a genuine widening of what a compromised session can do, and it is a policy decision, not a code one. Audit logging is required but is not a control.

F3 CANNOT BE PROVEN ANYWHERE. The contract states there is no QC host, cortex-2 is reserved for CORTEX /qc, and prod is the only Topic Manager box. F3's whole claim is that it survives install, upgrade AND reinstall - a fresh-install path and a migration path that will never have been executed before they reach prod. The 15 mode/ownership test cases also SKIP on this Windows workstation, since Git Bash cannot hold POSIX modes, and are only real via `bash tests/run.sh --remote <user>@<host> --strict`. A host for that is an unresolved operator decision carried over from WO-0001.

GATE COVERAGE - what does NOT cover this change: nothing checks the systemd unit file, the polkit rule, nginx, the new routes' authorisation, path containment on uploaded certs, the migration's idempotency, or the banner render. python-syntax and frontend-syntax see syntax only. The shell-syntax gate globs *.sh install/*.sh tools/*.sh tests/*.sh tests/lib/*.sh, so a helper placed anywhere else (install/helpers/, or a .rules file) is invisible to it. heredoc-python extracts only the three named anchors in upgrade-full.sh, so a new heredoc in the migration ships unparsed unless the anchor list grows. sbom-consistency and sca are unaffected unless requirements.txt moves. tools/check-config-example.sh will go RED by construction. Sonar remains unavailable (AppRole denied on secret/hooks/sonarqube).

CONTRACT DRIFT found while scoping: promote.prod.running_version says 1.0.0, but prod answered {"status":"ok","version":"1.0.3"} today. The surfaces[] note for app/main.js describes a hardcoded version fallback that no longer exists. app/components/TopBar.js:55 carries ?v=1003 and is not declared as a surface - it arrived in the last commit (0c08d1a) and has never been through a cascade.

AMBIGUITY needing a human answer: the brief says the restart button restarts BOTH services. nginx serves the request, so a true restart drops the in-flight response, whereas reload (SIGHUP) is graceful and is what an nginx CONFIG change needs. Under the decided 202-then-detach design the response is already flushed before either service is touched, so a hard restart is survivable - but it still breaks any other user's in-flight request, and nothing in v1.0.4 changes nginx's config, so restarting nginx buys nothing a reload does not. RECOMMENDATION: restart topic-manager, RELOAD nginx, and offer a hard nginx restart only behind an explicit checkbox. Confirm before builder implements 'restart both' literally. Sequencing regardless: flush the 202, then act on nginx first and topic-manager LAST, because restarting topic-manager kills the worker running the handler.

amendments: systemd/topic-manager-nginx-test.service - REQUIRED, and it widens D-1 from two units to three. MEASURED on prod 2026-09-01: `sudo -u topic-manager /usr/sbin/nginx -t` exits 1 with [emerg] open() "/run/nginx.pid" failed (13: Permission denied), and `-g 'pid /tmp/x.pid;'` is refused as a duplicate of nginx.conf line 3. `-e stderr` does not help. So the operator requirement 'nginx -t must pass before any nginx action' is unimplementable without a root-side test. A successful `systemctl reload nginx` is NOT a substitute: ExecReload is `nginx -s reload`, which exits 0 whether or not the master accepts the new config. The unit is Type=oneshot with a fixed absolute ExecStart in a root-owned file, reads configuration and writes nothing, and the polkit rule grants only 'start' on it. NEEDS OPERATOR SIGN-OFF.

builder.root_cause:
F2 was impossible rather than merely missing: the cluster list lived in config.yaml, which is root-owned 0640 root:topic-manager precisely so the application can read secret_key and never write it. Any app-writable cluster list therefore had to be a NEW file in a NEW directory - and making /etc/topic-manager itself writable was measured to let the app unlink the root-owned secrets file, because directory write IS unlink.
F1 was blocked by NoNewPrivileges=true, under which sudo cannot run at all; the D-Bus path survives it because the caller never escalates.
The staleness defect was TWO caches, not one: tm/config.py returned its first parse forever AND tm/app.py froze a second copy into app.config['TM_CONFIG'] that tm/routes._cfg() handed to every route. With four gunicorn workers, fixing either alone leaves a new cluster visible on about one request in four - which presents as a Kafka fault.
F4 was never a cosmetic flash. SettingsTab seeded 'UNCLASSIFIED'/'green' into the same data() fields saveBanner() reads, and loadSettings returned early on a non-ok response. An expired session plus one toggle therefore PUT those defaults over the operator's real banner, globally, for every user. The flash and the data loss are one root cause: defaults seeded into the fields the save path reads.

root_cause: ITEM 5 — the permission baseline was a LINE format over paths the attacker names. www-data owns /var/www/topic-manager, which record_baseline walks; a directory whose name ends in a newline lets find print an absolute path on the next line, and root replayed that as chown+chmod. The line format was the fault, not the parsing.

ITEM 6 — install -d on an existing path is chmod()+chown(), and both follow symlinks. cluster-certs sits under an app-owned parent inside ReadWritePaths, so the application chooses what root applies ownership to on the next run.

ITEM 7 — restart is a PERSISTENT STOP primitive, not a transient one: 5 starts in 10s trips systemd start limiting and the unit then refuses to start until a human runs reset-failed on the box. The route had no cooldown and no single-flight, and a module-level cache could not have provided either, because the four gunicorn workers share no memory.
ITEM 4 — nothing read the proxy headers, so every session row and login line recorded the loopback address: the audit trail could not answer the only question it exists for.
ITEM 3 — the ancestor assertion existed and was called on one branch of two.
ITEM 1 — the documented procedure told operators to create the directory root would read from, in /tmp, where the first account to create it owns it.
